::: {.why}
Most alternatives to the Sharpe ratio are the Sharpe ratio with extra sampling error, and knowing which ones carry independent information keeps you from reporting five numbers that say one thing.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say what Sortino changes about the denominator and what that costs in estimator precision.
- Report the correlation across strategies between Sharpe and each alternative, and say which alternative is not nearly redundant.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Test the redundancy empirically: build 200 random long-short signals on your universe, compute Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar and information ratio for each, and report the cross-strategy correlation matrix of the four. Two of them will be above 0.95 with Sharpe.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Compare precision: simulate at a known true Sharpe and compare the sampling standard deviation of Sharpe against Sortino at the same sample size. Downside deviation uses fewer observations, and the cost of that shows up here.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the conclusion into reports/milestone-02-noise-floor.md as a short table: which ratio you will report, which you will not, and why.
:::
:::
